From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>

Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, sarah.connors@acme.com
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Operational Sprint Snapshot + QBR asks (compact)

Team —

Quick pulse ahead of next week’s QBR prep run-through. Kept this tight: wins, risks, asks.

Wins:
- Dedicated rollout: Prod pool reached expected 95% utilization without latency spikes after the kernel tweak (PR#814).
- Eval pipeline: onboarding of two model families (mosaic v2 / redwood-lite) completed for internal perf tests; sample quality looks aligned with baseline.

Risks / open blockers:
- Capacity: Dedicated burst quota is still pending approval from finance for Nov–Dec commit. If not cleared, we lose predictable throughput for a key customer pilot (Acme).
- QBR narrative: we need a one-slide explanation of the cost/latency tradeoffs for the new quantization profiles — audience will ask for simple numbers.

Asks (owners & timing):
1) Karthik — finance approval status and any recommended wording for the Acme commit ask (deadline: Mon EOD).
2) Laura — can you sign off on the QBR one-pager narrative? I attached v2. If approved, I’ll lock visuals by Tue.
3) Marissa — pull final usage numbers (token-level) for the pilot: last 30 days by model variant (by Mon morning).

Attachments: QBR_onepager_v2.pdf, OKR_tracker_week45.xlsx (high-level tab only).

Short replies welcome — I’ll consolidate a single slide to feed into the exec deck.

Thanks,
Mina
Mina Haddad
Director, Program Ops | Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 08:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Operational Sprint Snapshot + QBR asks (compact)

Mina —

Thanks for the concise summary. Quick updates:
- Finance: I looped in procurement and FP&A this morning. There’s a short-form approval path for pilot-level commits; I expect an answer by Mon EOD as requested. If we need a longer commit, FP&A will want a 3-month usage forecast (I can draft).
- Acme ask: recommend wording that frames the burst as a safety buffer (so it reads like risk mitigation) rather than a permanent uplift. I’ll paste a 2-line boilerplate in a follow-up.

One operational note: if we land the burst but don’t enable automatic failover to hosted for overflow during holiday traffic, we should call that out in the slide.

On the QBR one-pager: the cost/latency numbers need a line that says "typical range (p50/p95) with quantized vs fp16" — ops team has a simple table we can include.

Karthik
VP, Finance & Commercial Ops
